@graph.name: How to Hire and Onboard a Senior Remote Software Engineer
@graph.description: A step-by-step guide to hiring, vetting, and onboarding a senior remote software engineer for your startup or product team.

step.name: Define your remote engineering requirements
step.text: Write a one-page spec: tech stack, scope, timeline, and communication expectations. Specify async vs. sync preference, timezone overlap needs, and whether you need full-stack or backend-only.

step.name: Evaluate async communication quality
step.text: Review their initial outreach email for clarity and specificity. Ask for a sample weekly update format. Check GitHub README quality — good documentation signals good async communication habits.

step.name: Assign a paid technical test
step.text: Give a 2–3 hour paid test with a clear spec and acceptance criteria. Evaluate: code quality, test coverage, documentation, and whether they ask clarifying questions before starting.

step.name: Agree on communication framework
step.text: Define: daily async update channel (Slack/WhatsApp), weekly written report format, Loom demo cadence, task tracking tool (Linear/GitHub Projects), and PR review SLA (24hr).

step.name: Secure onboarding and tooling access
step.text: Sign NDA and IP agreement. Set up GitHub access (branch protection enabled), secrets vault, staging environment, and communication channels before day one.

step.name: Start with a small defined task
step.text: First task: a small bug fix or feature with clear acceptance criteria. Their first PR reveals code quality, communication style, and integration ability better than any interview.

mainEntity.name: What does an async-first remote engineering workflow look like?

acceptedAnswer.text: Async-first workflow: written spec before code, daily async Slack updates, weekly written status report with PR links, Friday Loom demo, GitHub PRs for all changes, Linear/GitHub Projects for task tracking. Works across any timezone difference.

mainEntity.name: How do you handle timezone differences with US or EU clients?

acceptedAnswer.text: Based in Nepal (UTC+5:45) with overlap windows for US East (8:45 AM–12:45 PM EST), US West (8:00 AM–12:00 PM PST), and UK/EU (9:00 AM–1:00 PM GMT). Async-first means timezone differences create a 24-hour development cycle without anyone working nights.

mainEntity.name: When should I hire a remote engineer on retainer vs hourly vs fixed-price?

acceptedAnswer.text: Hourly: exploratory work, audits, undefined scope. Monthly retainer ($1,999/mo): ongoing product development with consistent 40hr/week needs. Fixed-price (from $5,499): defined features or MVPs with clear acceptance criteria. Pre-PMF → hourly. Post-PMF → retainer. Defined scope → fixed-price.
